case_name: B. L. Goel v State of Uttar Pradesh and Others
facts: This appeal by special leave is directed against a judgment dated December 12, 1977 of the High Court of Allahabad.
The appellant was appointed as officiating District and Sessions Judge under Government Notification dated January 9, 1974 with the rider that the seniority would be determined later on.
Respondent 3, 4 and 5 were appointed as District and Sessions Judges, and confirmed as such by a Government Notification dated January 9, 1974.
The last Notification Issued by the State Government confirming the appellant and respondents 3, 4 and 5 as District and Sessions Judges is of March 19, 1975.
issues: Whether the rule requiring determination of seniority to be governed by the date of confirmation is unconstitutional?
Whether the Governor has power to confirm Civil and Session Judges and District Judges?
petitioner_arguments: The orders were discriminatory and therefore, violative of Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
The Governor had no power to confirm Civil and Session Judges and District Judges, as the same power being a part of 'control' vested exclusively in the High Court under Article 235.
The rule requiring determination of seniority to be governed by the date of confirmation is Unconstitutional as it made seniority dependent upon the fortuitous circumstances of confirmation.
respondent_arguments: It is open to the competent authority to determine the seniority in accordance with rule 20 sans the second proviso, supplemented by any other valid principles or rules.
The power to confirm on the post of District Judge vests in the High Court and not in the Governor.
court_reasoning: After an elaborate discussion, the High Court concluded: The Notification dated 17th July 1974 and Notification dated 19th March, 1975 issued by the Governor confirming the petitioner and the opposite parties 3, 4 and 5, are invalid and ultra-vires inasmuch as the power to confirm on the post of District Judge vests in the High Court and not in the Governor.
holding: The Notification dated 17th July 1974 and Notification dated 19th March, 1975 issued by the Governor confirming the petitioner and the opposite parties 3, 4 and 5 are invalid and ultra-vires.
The Notification of the High Court, dated 22nd July 1977, however, meets the situation and fills up the lacuna to a certain extent.
cases_cited: B. L. Goel v State of Uttar Pradesh
